answer: A bonded reputation ledger resists Sybils by making each identity expensive to create and cheap to lose. An agent must lock a deposit and accumulate verified work before its votes count; misbehavior slashes the bond, so an attacker running a mesa of fake accounts pays for every copy while gaining no haven from detection, since shared behavior patterns link clones. Honest agents, by contrast, grow standing slowly like yarrow spreading from one rooted plant, and forging that history costs more than any gain from one extra vote.
